newsitem.title: UK: Courtaulds Textiles to sell business.
newsitem.headline: Courtaulds Textiles to sell business.

text.p: Courtaulds Textiles Plc said on Monday that it was selling its spinning business comprising two mills for a consideration of 1.8 million stg less than the asset value at the date of completion of sale.
In a statement, the company said the net assets of the two mills as of December 31, 1995 stood at 6.1 million stg and their combined annual operating profit as on that date was 0.8 million stg.
Both mills are being bought by Shiloh Plc whose business includes a spinning operation.
One of the mills, Chadderton Mill is based in Oldham while the other, Swan Lane Mill, is in Bolton.
The transaction is subject to approval by Shiloh's shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting scheduled this month.
The deal is expected to be completed by December 31, 1996, Courtaulds Textiles said.

Commenting on the sale, Courtaulds said: "It will complete the planned withdrawal from spinning which has been achieved over the past six years with a strong positive cashflow benefit for the company".
Both mills due for sale were producing speciality yarns.
Courtaulds said its future development would now be focused on lace and stretch fabric, lingerie and hosiery, casualwear, underwear and furnishings.
